shorts.hook: Ice once trapped a lake bigger than two Great Lakes combined.
shorts.title: An Ice Dam Burst and Flooded Washington Dozens of Times
shorts.outro: What happens next is even worse. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: Glacial Lake Missoula held about as much water as Lake Erie and Lake Ontario combined, emptied in about two days when its ice dam failed, and then refilled and did it again dozens of times.

shorts.hook: The Thames once froze solid enough to hold a street fair.
shorts.title: The Thames Used to Freeze Partly Because of a Bridge
shorts.outro: Then it gets much colder. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: The last Thames frost fair filled about a kilometer of frozen river in 1814, the old nineteen-arch London Bridge helped the ice form, and Doug buys a printed souvenir card right before the thaw.

shorts.hook: Two point four billion years ago, microbes started breathing out oxygen.
shorts.title: Oxygen-Making Microbes May Have Frozen the Whole Planet
shorts.outro: It only gets colder from here. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: Around 2.4 billion years ago, oxygen from microbes destroyed the methane keeping Earth warm, and some geologists think it set off the first Snowball Earth.
